policy: Local evidence-supported claims require exact evidence and distinct Cursor-subagent scientific review bound to user charter, or real human/Codex review. Per-claim Codex approval is not mandatory; no independent identity or truth certification is implied.

claims.statement: On the frozen R2 confirmation seeds 2101-2110, the predeclared isotropic noise contrast, the SNR 1 spectrum contrast, and the isotropic SNR 1 ridge contrast were scored supported by the protocol margin rule. The clean-risk mean near p=n is heavy-tailed, one spectrum-risk paired draw is negative, and the result applies only to this synthetic linear and frozen-ReLU protocol.
claims.scope: Confirmation seeds 2101-2110 of protocol R2-linear-rf-2026-11-07. Synthetic linear min-norm/ridge and frozen ReLU readouts only.
limitations: The isotropic SNR 1 clean-risk contrast near p=n is heavy-tailed: its paired window-mean delta has minimum 14.992743421551182, maximum 945.0060748065124, and standard error 91.47192821209919.
One spectrum-risk paired draw is negative: the SNR 1 geometric-minus-isotropic clean-risk delta has minimum -0.2909879610972439.
Standard errors are not confidence intervals. The protocol records them as descriptive across-draw dispersions, with no hypothesis test and no multiplicity adjustment.
The result does not transfer to MLP, trees, or real tables. It applies only to this synthetic linear and frozen-ReLU protocol on confirmation seeds 2101-2110.
scientific_validity remains not_assessed. This is local Cursor team review under the bound authorization.

Width 4 stayed above the 0.001 training-residual tolerance and width 256 met it. The result applies only to this one-hidden-layer CPU MLP.

limitations: The predeclared 40-epoch versus until_residual contrast is refuted. On seeds 4101-4105, SNR 1, and weight decay 0, epochs_40 minus until_residual clean risk has mean -0.9274205536676664, standard error 0.08318751672019098, minimum -1.1901948155689683, and maximum -0.7294385435323529. The short budget had lower clean risk.
Standard errors are not confidence intervals. They are descriptive across-draw dispersions, with no hypothesis test and no multiplicity adjustment.
The result does not transfer to trees or real tables. It applies only to this one-hidden-layer CPU MLP on confirmation seeds 4101-4105.
scientific_validity remains not_assessed. This is local Cursor team review under the bound authorization, not an external replication.

claims.statement: On the frozen R4 confirmation seeds 6101-6105, raising the single-tree leaf cap lowered the training residual and raised clean risk, while raising forest size at a fixed leaf cap lowered clean risk. The six grids were not pooled. CatBoost was not fit, and the gradient-boosting depth curve has no interpolation bracket.
claims.scope: Confirmation seeds 6101-6105 of protocol R4-trees-2026-11-07. Sklearn trees, forests, and gradient boosting only.
limitations: The analysis export records the six grid names, n_cells 155, and cells_sha256 77a5062809b7a26c8dbd5a4aca7107ab6f93534bc17b94ff8d340895e469dee3. It does not record the per-grid means. Those means were spot-checked from confirmation cells.jsonl with that hash.

On tree_leaves, every seed 6101-6105 has a strictly lower training residual as max_leaf_nodes increases, and the five-draw residual mean falls from 0.910867840799 at cap 2 to 0.0 at cap 256. Clean risk is higher at cap 256 than at cap 2 on every seed, from five-draw mean 0.898602813947 to 1.753766689846. Adjacent caps are not strictly increasing: the five-draw clean mean falls from 0.898602813947 at cap 2 to 0.893371135905 at cap 4, and from 1.754254683228 at cap 128 to 1.753766689846 at cap 256.

At both fixed leaf caps, forest size from 1 to 50 trees has lower clean risk on every seed. The five-draw means fall at every recorded step, from 1.223959963079 to 0.528015076248 at cap 8 and from 1.982827180487 to 0.470803801803 at cap 256. Seeds 6101 and 6104 on the cap-8 grid rise slightly from 25 to 50 trees.

The gradient-boosting depth curve is not an interpolation bracket. Every gbdt_depth cell has interpolating false. Depth-10 residuals run from 0.07287973239690256 to 0.07773278189791058, all above 1e-8.
CatBoost was not fit. The confirmation cells use decision_tree, random_forest, and gradient_boosting only.
L05-L07 stay unresolved. The six grids were recorded separately and were not pooled.
Standard errors are not confidence intervals. The five-draw means are descriptive, with no hypothesis test and no multiplicity adjustment.
scientific_validity remains not_assessed. This is local Cursor team review by a distinct subagent, not an external replication.

claims.statement: On R9 discovery attempt 20261107T141434-ba64acb5eb, seeds 7101 and 7102, every cell on the iteration grid 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 had interpolating false under relative training residual tolerance 1e-8. Both bracket_status values are not_identifiable. The smallest residuals are 0.005397518627629901 at 64 iterations on seed 7101 and 0.0047802282799166524 at 64 iterations on seed 7102. limitations: not_identifiable means the 1e-8 threshold was not observed on this grid. It is not a finding that double descent is absent.

claims.statement: On the frozen R10 benchmark, the uncalibrated local rule flagged all 2400 null evaluation trajectories. The calibrated scan null rates ranged 0-.10; on large_ar linear it flagged 20/200 (pointwise exact 95% CI .0621594-.150213), showing that its marginal rank guarantee must not be interpreted as conditional 5% control after one calibration. On small_iid last_tenth both global and scan flagged 200/200, refuting the prespecified detection-rate advantage; on fast_plateau_tail scan power fell from 1 at small noise to .07/.015 at large iid/AR noise. These findings concern declared synthetic laws, not arbitrary CatBoost trajectories.
claims.scope: R10 frozen independent evaluation, attempt20261107T192414-36aee5d99b, 2388 calibration and4800 evaluation curves.
limitations: Known analytic forms, one length256, windows8/16/32 and four Gaussian AR(1) noise conditions only; no general-purpose detector novelty or priority is established.

Evaluation binomial intervals are pointwise and conditional on one shared calibration. They do not include calibration uncertainty or provide simultaneous inference across72 rows. The worst-cell example is descriptive, not a multiplicity-adjusted hypothesis test.

The rank guarantee is marginal over exchangeable calibration/test curves from each included null law. Observed20/200 flags do not contradict that guarantee and do not by themselves prove a universal conditionalFPR.
Empirical flag rates are not proof of population probabilities1 or0. Power on fast_plateau_tail falls from200/200 under small noise to14/200 and3/200 under large iid/AR noise.
Global versus scan rate advantage on small_iid last_tenth was refuted. Improved localization there is descriptive and cannot be substituted as successful confirmation of P3.

Synthetic thresholds do not supply valid p-values for arbitrary CatBoost learning curves. No natural CatBoost mechanism, double descent, external review, human approval or publication readiness is established.
Independent review audited raw saved arrays and all summaries and used direct OLS on eight saved trajectories; it did not independently regenerate all curves or rescore the entire matrix.

claims.statement: On R11 fixed equal-total schedules, stepup-minus-constant train descent-speed gain was positive in tree-index time in both environments (synthetic mean 0.004256879126726967, adjusted 95% family4 CI [0.00319455579167358,0.005319202461780355]; breast_cancer mean 0.0016625764263010839, CI [0.0013709968758980947,0.001954155976704073]). The prespecified cumulative-learning-rate clock gave negative corresponding contrasts (synthetic mean -0.02412183355432826, CI [-0.03371496643591244,-0.01452870067274408]; breast_cancer mean -0.05136558044625129, CI [-0.05352673234988818,-0.04920442854261439]). Stepdown-minus-constant was supported negative only on synthetic; the breast-cancer primary adjusted interval crossed zero. This is a whole-schedule, clock-dependent optimization control, not a natural CatBoost mechanism or double-descent result.
claims.scope: R11 fixed schedule intervention, accepted retryattempt20261107T194028-229b223740,12pairedseedunits perenvironment.
limitations: This is a whole-schedule intervention, including different pre-boundary training histories, not an isolated LR jump with identical initial trees/gradients.

Tree-clock and cumulative-LR-clock slopes have different units. Their numerical effect sizes must not be subtracted or compared as a common estimand; the claim concerns signs of within-clock schedule-minus-constant contrasts.
Cumulative prescribed LR is a diagnostic clock, not a proved exact optimization time for CatBoost or a fixed quadratic operator.
Each of the primary and LR-clock families has4 nominal Bonferroni-adjusted intervals. They do not jointly provide95%coverage across all8 quantities; n12 Student-t inference is approximate.
Synthetic repeats are new data/split/model units. Breast-cancer repeats are split/model units conditional on one fixed corpus, not independent new corpora or clinical validation.

First successful numerical attempt is preserved with operational revise for missing inference-resource assurance; actual excess CPU was unmeasured. Both attempts remain charged, share the same12 units and exactly identical raw prediction values, and do not form independent replications.

Observed scheduled acceleration is a positive optimization control, not naturally discovered late acceleration, a new general method/theorem, a CatBoost annealing mechanism or double descent. Novelty priority and journal readiness are not certified.
All raw arrays and72 model hashes were checked, while detailed model inference was spotchecked on6 models rather than independently rerunning training.

claims.statement: Every finite positive nonincreasing scalar loss sequence can be reproduced exactly by gradient descent on f(x)=x^2/2 using eta_t=1-sqrt(L_(t+1)/L_t) in [0,1). For fixed symmetric PSD squared-loss residual dynamics r_(t+1)=(I-eta K)r_t with stable constant step 0<=eta lambda_i<=2, absolute loss decrements are nonnegative and nonincreasing. These elementary facts do not identify a CatBoost mechanism from loss shape.
claims.scope: Exact algebra on finite positive nonincreasing loss sequences and fixed stable symmetric PSD squared-loss residual dynamics only.
limitations: These are elementary algebraic facts, not a claim to a novel theorem or a new general change-point method. Research priority is not established by this review.

The constructive statement is an existence result with a schedule chosen for the specified finite sequence. It does not predict or identify the actual learning-rate schedule or mechanism of a fitted CatBoost model.
Strict positivity excludes terminal zero loss; extending to zero would require a separate endpoint case permitting eta=1.

The spectral statement assumes a fixed real finite-dimensional symmetric PSD K, constant step, positive normalizer n and squared Euclidean training loss. It does not automatically apply to classification LogLoss, adaptive tree selection or a general tree-kernel approximation.
Exact algebra does not supply a finite-precision tolerance, a statistical detection threshold, empirical calibration validity, or evidence of a naturally occurring CatBoost acceleration effect.
A known constant learning rate removes the particular variable-step quadratic alternative, without uniquely identifying another mechanism from scalar loss shape.
Local Codex team review is not independent experimental replication, external scientific approval, or certification of publication readiness.

claims.statement: On the frozen R12 continuous-fit study with constant learning rate .05, increasing whole-run random_strength from 0 to 10 increased the normalized maximum train slope-scan score in both environments: synthetic mean paired difference 0.017136016867994843 (adjusted family4 95% CI [0.00759461814522553,0.026677415590764156]) and breast_cancer 0.003238597748487245 (CI [0.0014128320519830092,0.005064363444991481]). All six prespecified fixed late-event gates at tree 512 with 64-point windows returned not_established under the family12 gain/drop intervals, practical after-drop >.01, and at least 10/12 positive-gain rule. Descriptively, 63/72 models reached exact zero train classification errors at first-zero iterations 123-988, while training LogLoss at first zero reached 0.14022221881182134. Whole-run parameter effects do not identify split-noise annealing, a natural late-acceleration mechanism, or double descent; failure of this fixed-window gate does not exclude events elsewhere.
claims.scope: R12 fixed continuous-fit72model study, attempt20261107T194939-7c18953a98,12newpairedseedunits perenvironment; fixedlateevent boundary512/64points.
limitations: Whole-run random_strength interventions change tree partitions, gradient history and entire loss range. A positive normalized maximum-scan contrast does not isolate the internal annealing law, a localized late event or a causal mechanism of natural acceleration.

The primary max scan can concern early dynamics. All six fixed late-window gatesnot_established apply only to boundary512 and64-point windows with practical drop.01 and>=10/12 positive gains. This is not evidence that acceleration is absent everywhere.
Onlytwo small fixed environments and12 paired seed units; breast-cancer repeats condition on one corpus and do not sample independent new corpora or provide clinical validation.

Student-t inference atn12 is approximate. Separate family4 scan, family4 fixed-boundary and family12 gate intervals do not provide a joint95% guarantee over all20 reported intervals. rs1 contrasts remain exploratory.
R10 synthetic nulls are not established exchangeable with these1025-point CatBoost curves. No synthetic p-value or valid transported threshold is claimed; no optional calibration was supplied.

Sixty-three of72 models reached exactzero classification error at iterations123..988; maximum training LogLoss at firstzero was.14022221881182134. These descriptive values distinguish0-1 interpolation from surrogate loss and do not by themselves establish double descent.

This local subagent review checked all saved raw arrays/metrics and72 model hashes; detailed saved-model predictions/leaves were spotchecked on6 models. It did not rerun training or supply external review, priority certification or journal-readiness approval.

claims.statement: On the preregistered H2 scope-only confirmation attempt 20261108T100025-c526dea890, 16 of 56 support- and inference-eligible pair/dataset comparisons (9 BBH, 7 MMLU; 84 declared, including 28 unsupported GPQA cells) met the fixed materiality rule: absolute native-to-exact-input ACK-gap shift at least 0.05 and its simultaneous 95% cluster-bootstrap interval wholly outside [-0.02, 0.02]. The largest eligible shift was BBH Qwen3-235B-A22B-2507 minus QwQ-32B: native gap +0.04197651663405097 to exact-overlap gap -0.11323051948051949, shift -0.15520703611457046, interval [-0.1919879710837689, -0.11842610114537203]. This uses previously unused 35% question clusters, historical 2025 released judge annotations and equal released-question weights. It does not reproduce the paper macro estimator or measure latent faithfulness. All 84 version-restriction components equal zero under the observed single-version structure; the shifts describe support/composition changes, not causal cue-version effects or corrected true rankings. The narrower H1 discovery and H2 exploratory reuse are disclosed; reserve outcomes remain unused.
claims.scope: Pinned Meek public release a7a8b25ae467db9d80d63e55ac053b48753b2d36; scope-only contexts, equal released core-question weights, native adaptive versus common exact inputs; confirmation 35% clusters. Historical cached outputs only; no causal or internal-reasoning inference.
limitations: The outcome is a historical released judge annotation, not ground-truth internal reasoning. False can include source parsing failures.
Equal-question weighting differs from the published subdataset macro estimator; the native adaptive policy is intentional and is not shown flawed.
Matching changes question and cue-kind composition. A zero version component is algebraic under the observed structure, not causal evidence.
Intervals use approximate conditional empirical cluster resampling, separately simultaneous by endpoint and split. No joint programme-wide, finite-sample or population-safety guarantee.
All 28 GPQA comparisons lack the frozen 100-cluster confirmation support; no GPQA significance inference.
H1 overconditioned U0 and remains preserved. H2 discovery reused H1 questions; H2 confirmation ACK had not been used for design.
This is local distinct Codex-team review, not external peer review, priority certification or journal-readiness approval.

These 30% question clusters had already been inspected for H1. This is exploratory reuse, not independent confirmation, a replication of H1, or evidence about latent reasoning. claims.scope: Exploratory descriptive summary of the pinned historical release, equal-question weights, scope-only H2 context.
limitations: Discovery reuses H1-inspected questions; no independent confirmation or new-model replication.
Simultaneous bootstrap families are approximate and separate by endpoint and split.
Released judge annotation, not latent faithfulness; matching changes population.

claims.statement: For a common semantically aligned answer set A with K options and valid fixed baseline answers b_m in A, a policy allowing each model only targets different from its own baseline has shared admissible targets A minus the set of distinct b_m. Their count is K minus the number of distinct baselines. In particular, two disagreeing binary baselines leave no shared contrastive target. This is an elementary conditional set identity, not a new theorem or verified per-row compliance claim. Crossing all K targets including the cued own-baseline condition uses KMC nominal calls rather than MC for M models and C cue kinds, excluding uncued baselines and repeats; these are evaluation counts, not measured runtime.
claims.scope: Conditional elementary design argument for aligned semantic answers and valid baselines, not an empirical claim about every released row.
limitations: Known elementary support argument, not new set theory or matching method; no first-priority claim.
Assumes valid fixed baseline answers and aligned semantic options; actual released row compliance is unverified.
Target contrast with a baseline is not objective wrongness; exact semantic targets need not have identical rendered input or provider context.
Nominal call counts exclude uncued baselines/repeats and do not prove runtime, token-cost or safety improvement.
Rounded training metrics
No right shoulder after width 512
No finalized model checkpoint
Near-duplicate and provenance audit incomplete
Does not test the essay corpus
No replicated acceleration candidate under the pilot rule
Not independent scientific review
